explanation: Erdős #1189, part 1: how many irreducible covering sets of size k are there? Covering sets (distinct moduli > 1, one residue each, covering ℤ) and irreducibility (no proper covering subset) are encoded correctly. There are finitely many of each size, since n_k ≤ 2^{k−1} (Simpson). "How many" is read as an asymptotic for log I(k), which is a reasonable and documented interpretation. The statement is faithful and open.
